summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease, bilateral lower extremity amputations, and a history of recurrent C. difficile infections was admitted after being found unresponsive by EMS. She had severe hypoglycemia with a blood glucose of 16, likely due to an insulin dosing error, and was treated with dextrose via her dialysis line. She also presented with hypotension and dehydration, thought to be secondary to recent C. difficile colitis and inadequate oral intake. Stool testing confirmed toxigenic C. difficile, and she was started on a tapered course of oral vancomycin. Initial concern for a multidrug-resistant urinary tract infection led to empiric antibiotics, but these were discontinued when cultures showed low bacterial counts and no signs of sepsis. Her dialysis catheter was replaced prior to discharge as a preventive measure. She remained hemodynamically stable, restarted her heart medications, and was discharged home in improved condition with medication adjustments and close follow-up planned.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
